message.content:
Here’s the exact API request you’d send to pull just the **IDs** and **context** attributes for community comments on `test4.org`, using your continuation cursor and API key:

```http
GET https://api.yourservice.com/v1/community/comments
    ?domain=test4.org
    &cursor=cur456
    &fields=id,context
    &apikey=key123
```

### What each part does

| Query Parameter | Purpose |
|-----------------|---------|
| `domain` | Filters comments to those belonging to `test4.org`. |
| `cursor` | Tells the API to continue from the point indicated by `cur456`. |
| `fields` | Limits the response payload to only the `id` and `context` fields (no other comment data). |
| `apikey` | Authenticates the request with your key (`key123`). |

### Example cURL command

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/community/comments?domain=test4.org&cursor=cur456&fields=id,context&apikey=key123"
```

### Expected JSON response

```json
{
  "comments": [
    { "id": "cmt001", "context": { /* context data */ } },
    { "id": "cmt002", "context": { /* context data */ } }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cur789"   // if more pages exist
}
```

Just replace `https://api.yourservice.com` with the actual base URL of your API provider. This will return only the IDs and context attributes for the requested community comments.
